Consider a directed weighted graph G(V, E), where V is the set of vertices and E is the set of edges. Suppose we use adjacency list to implement the graph. Consider a sequence of |V| operations with each corresponding to a different vertex in V. For the operation for vertex v, the cost is assumed to be the number of outgoing edges from v.  (a) What is the cost of the worst possible single operation in this sequence of operations? (b) What is the average amortized cost of the above sequence of operations based on aggregate analysis?

message.content:
In a directed graph with |V| vertices, the worst possible single operation occurs when a vertex has the maximum possible out-degree, which is |V| - 1, meaning one operation can cost as much as |V| - 1.

The aggregate analysis for the entire sequence of |V| operations reveals that the total cost across all operations equals |E|, since the sum of all out-degrees in the graph is exactly the total number of edges.

* The worst-case cost of a single operation is |V| - 1, which is achieved when a vertex has edges to every other vertex in the graph.
* The average amortized cost per operation, computed via aggregate analysis, is |E| / |V|, since the total cost of all |V| operations is |E| and the average is the total cost divided by the number of operations.
